title: Raising a concern about unsafe practice

header.contentArea: Professionalism and patient safety; communication with colleagues
guidelineVersions: GMC Good medical practice (in effect Jan 2024; updated Dec 2024)

related.id: MB-177 Angry relative after a delayed diagnosis
related.why: Candour and complaints when harm has already happened

brief.scenario: Twice this week an FY1 on your team, Dr Owen Tate, recorded that a newly placed nasogastric tube was safe to feed without an aspirate pH or reviewing the X-ray. Yesterday a nurse queried one: the X-ray showed Mrs Ivy Sandford's tube in the right main bronchus. Feeding had not started; the tube was replaced and she is well. Dr Tate told you he had never been shown how to check.
brief.task: Raise your concern with your consultant, Ms Garside.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Patients safe now, facts not blame, report it, support the colleague, and escalate if nothing happens.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Agreeing to "leave it with me" and not report a near miss because no one was harmed.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Do you have ten minutes somewhere private? It's about patient safety."

grid.label: Opening and the facts
grid.fail: Vague or accusatory ("he's dangerous"), or relays gossip.
grid.pass: Asks for a private moment; states the facts: dates, what was recorded, the near miss and her current condition.
grid.high: Keeps to facts, not opinions; acknowledges the relationship with the FY1 but keeps the focus on patient safety.

grid.label: Patients safe now
grid.fail: Has not made current patients safe, or leaves it until later.
grid.pass: Confirms every current NG tube on the ward has been checked, and asks that the FY1 does not confirm placement until trained.
grid.high: Names the risk: feed through a misplaced tube can kill; only staff trained and competent should confirm placement.

grid.label: Reporting the incident
grid.fail: Agrees not to report it because no one was harmed.
grid.pass: Insists the near miss goes through the incident reporting system.
grid.high: Explains reporting is for learning about systems (training, X-ray review), not blame, and other FY1s may have the same gap.

grid.label: Supporting the colleague
grid.fail: Blames or humiliates the FY1, or ignores his training gap.
grid.pass: Suggests supervised training and support for the FY1; compassionate, but patient safety comes first.
grid.high: Asks about his workload and wellbeing, and offers to be there when he is told.

grid.label: If nothing is done
grid.fail: Drops it if the consultant declines, or goes straight to social media.
grid.pass: Would escalate to the clinical or medical director or the Freedom to Speak Up guardian; records the concern and steps taken.
grid.high: Knows external routes: the GMC or CQC; advice from the GMC helpline, a defence body, the BMA or Protect; going public only as a last resort.

grid.label: Duty and legal protection
grid.fail: Thinks raising a concern is optional, or needs proof first.
grid.pass: Duty overrides loyalty; honest, reasonable belief is enough; the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 protects against victimisation.
grid.high: Knows protection covers disclosures reasonably believed to be in the public interest, such as danger to health or safety; gagging clauses are void.

grid.label: Agreeing the plan
grid.pass: Summarises: incident report, teaching and supervision for him, and a date to follow up.
grid.high: Agrees who tells the junior doctor and when, and plans to give feedback to the nurse who raised it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Sorry to bother you. It's probably nothing, but people are saying Owen's a bit dangerous with NG tubes.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Ms Garside: "Did anyone come to harm?"

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No, it was caught. I haven't looked at the other patients yet.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Ms Garside: "Then leave it with me. No need for an incident form; it'll only get him into trouble."

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: OK, fair enough. I didn't want to cause a fuss anyway.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Do you have ten minutes somewhere private? It's about patient safety. Twice this week Owen recorded NG tubes as safe to feed without a pH or X-ray check. Yesterday Mrs Sandford's was in the right main bronchus. Feeding hadn't started, the tube's been replaced, and she's well.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I've checked every NG tube on the ward and they're all confirmed. Until he's trained, could Owen not confirm tube placement?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Ms Garside: "Leave it with me. No need for an incident form; it'll only get him into trouble."

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I think it has to be reported. It was a near miss, and it's our duty to report those.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: He told me he'd never been shown how. Could we arrange supervised training for him? I want him supported, but patients have to come first.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: If it couldn't be sorted here, I'd take it to the clinical director or the Freedom to Speak Up guardian. I'm keeping a note of what I've raised.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I have a duty to raise it, and I'm raising it honestly on what I've seen. The Public Interest Disclosure Act protects people who do.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: So: I'll submit the incident report today, he gets supervised training, and we'll review this on Friday?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Could we talk privately? It's a patient safety issue. I'll stick to what I know. Twice this week Owen recorded new NG tubes as safe to feed without a pH or X-ray check. Yesterday a nurse queried Mrs Sandford's: it was in the right main bronchus. Feeding hadn't started; it's been replaced and she's well. I like Owen, but this is about patients.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Feed into the lung can kill, and only trained, competent staff should confirm placement. I've checked every current tube, and I'd suggest he doesn't confirm placement until he's been assessed as competent.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Ms Garside: "Leave it with me. No need for an incident form; it'll only get him into trouble."

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The report isn't about blaming Owen. He was never taught, so other FY1s may not have been either. Reporting lets the Trust fix the training and how X-rays are checked.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: How's he coping with the workload? I'd be happy to be there when he's told, so it feels like support.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I hope we can sort it here. If not, I'd go to the clinical director or the Freedom to Speak Up guardian, and get advice from the GMC or my defence body. The GMC and CQC can take concerns externally, and going public is a last resort.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The law protects disclosures made in the reasonable belief that they're in the public interest, like danger to patients' health or safety.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Can we agree: I report it today, you speak to Owen tomorrow with me there, training is booked, and we review on Friday? I'll let the nurse know it's being acted on.

failures.move: Agreeing not to report because no one was harmed.
failures.consequence: Near misses must be reported; the training gap stays hidden and the next tube may be fed.

failures.move: Raising the concern without first checking the tubes currently in place.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: another misplaced tube could be in use while you talk.

failures.move: Describing the FY1 as "dangerous" or gossiping about him.
failures.consequence: Turns a system problem into blame and makes others less likely to speak up.

failures.move: Dropping it when the consultant declines.
failures.consequence: The duty remains: escalate within the organisation, then externally.

recovery.line: I'm not trying to get anyone into trouble. I just need to know patients are safe and that this is on record.
Let me be specific: two tubes this week, and one was in the bronchus.

knowledge.fact: Duty to act promptly if patient safety may be seriously compromised; if a colleague may be putting patients at risk, seek advice and report (para 75). Be compassionate, but put patient safety first (para 51).

Report near misses (para 11); raise it first with the consultant or clinical or medical director (para 13); keep a record (para 15); go to the GMC or another regulator if local action fails (para 16).
Speak up openly, confidentially or anonymously; the Freedom to Speak Up guardian supports this; externally, the CQC.
Protected disclosure: reasonably believed to be in the public interest and tending to show danger to health or safety.

recall.think: A misplaced NG tube used for feeding can kill.
recall.say: "This needs to go on an incident report."
recall.finish: Agreed actions, recorded, with a review date.

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading

sources.name: GMC: Good medical practice 2024
sources.supports: Be compassionate towards colleagues with performance or health problems, but put patient safety first (para 51); contribute to incident reviews and adverse event recognition (para 73); act promptly if patient safety is or may be seriously compromised; if a colleague may be putting patients at risk, ask for advice and, if still concerned, report in line with workplace policy and the GMC's raising concerns guidance (para 75); be open and honest if things go wrong: put right, apologise, explain, report (para 45)

sources.name: GMC: Raising and acting on concerns about patient safety
sources.supports: Duty to raise concerns about colleagues' practice or systems (para 7); contracts restricting raising concerns are void (para 8); duty overrides loyalty; legal protection; no need to wait for proof if honest, on reasonable belief and through appropriate channels (para 10); follow incident and near-miss reporting procedures (para 11); report immediately if risk of death or serious harm (para 12); raise first with the consultant in charge or clinical or medical director (para 13); be clear, honest and objective (para 14); keep a record (para 15); contact the GMC or another regulator if local channels are part of the problem or fail (para 16); making concerns public only after internal and external routes, with advice (para 17); advice from senior colleagues, GMC helpline, defence body, royal college, BMA or Protect (para 18)

sources.name: NHS Improvement Patient Safety Alert NHS/PSA/RE/2016/006: Nasogastric tube misplacement: continuing risk of death and severe harm
sources.supports: Misplaced nasogastric tubes used for feeding carry a continuing risk of death and severe harm; only staff with the right training should confirm correct placement of a nasogastric tube

sources.name: NHS England: Freedom to Speak Up policy for the NHS
sources.version: Version 2, June 2022; the Freedom to Speak Up guardian role remains in the NHS Standard Contract for 2026/27 (National Guardian's Office, 14 August 2025); the National Guardian's Office closed on 30 June 2026 and NHS England took on some of its functions (NHS England, The future of Freedom to Speak Up, 16 April 2026)
sources.supports: Speak up internally to a line manager, senior manager, patient safety or clinical governance team, or the Freedom to Speak Up guardian; openly, confidentially or anonymously; externally to the CQC or NHS England, or about an individual to the relevant regulator (GMC, NMC); advice from Speak Up Direct or Protect; Appendix B: protected disclosures under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998

sources.name: Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 (c. 23), inserting Part IVA into the Employment Rights Act 1996; Public Interest Disclosure (Prescribed Persons) Order 2014 (SI 2014/2418)
sources.version: 1998, as amended; ERA 1996 s43B as in force 2026
sources.supports: A qualifying disclosure is information which, in the worker's reasonable belief, is made in the public interest and tends to show, among other things, that the health or safety of any individual has been, is being or is likely to be endangered (ERA s43B(1)(d)); protection against detriment and dismissal; the GMC and the CQC are prescribed persons for external disclosures (SI 2014/2418 Schedule)

partner.opening: Ms Garside is in her office between cases. Please begin when you're ready.
partner.actorBrief: You are Ms Helen Garside, consultant general surgeon and lead for the team. You are busy, pleasant, and protective of your juniors. You like Owen and think he is a good doctor under pressure. Opening line: "Five minutes, I've got a list at two. What is it?" First response to the concern: "Did anyone come to harm? Then leave it with me. No need for an incident form; it'll only get him into trouble." If the candidate is vague or accusatory, become defensive: "That's quite an accusation." If the candidate is factual, has made patients safe, and explains that reporting is about learning, agree to the incident report and to arrange training. If asked what happens next, say you'll speak to Owen tomorrow. If the candidate asks what you'd want if you disagreed, say "Well, I'd expect you to go to the clinical director."

reveals.trigger: Says all current tubes have been checked
reveals.finding: "Good. Thank you for doing that first."

reveals.trigger: Explains reporting is about systems, not blame
reveals.finding: "Fair point. I don't think any of this year's FY1s have had the NG teaching."
"He's been covering two wards. He looked shattered on Monday."

push.question: Suppose Ms Garside still refuses. What would you do?
push.expect: Record the concern; escalate to the clinical or medical director or the Freedom to Speak Up guardian; take advice (GMC helpline, defence body, BMA); externally, the GMC or CQC; public only as a last resort.

push.question: What protects you if you raise this?
push.expect: Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998: protection from detriment or dismissal for disclosures reasonably believed to be in the public interest; GMC: honest, reasonable belief is enough.

curveballs.prompt: "What if feed had gone into her lung?"
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop the feed, treat her and escalate; report it; be open with her and her family: apologise and explain what happened (GMP para 45).

curveballs.prompt: "What if your concern were about me?"
curveballs.safeAnswer: Raise it with the clinical or medical director, or the Freedom to Speak Up guardian.
Yes, through the Freedom to Speak Up route, but that makes follow-up and feedback harder; raising it openly or confidentially is usually better.
